summary: Learn QGIS hazard mapping, satellite-layer interpretation and warning-area workflows. Explore the 10-day course outline and see if it fits your role.
lede: GIS for radiological safety and monitoring uses spatial data to support warning coordination and response planning, not technical radiation assessment. For GIS officers, disaster-risk professionals and emergency planners, the course covers preparing hazard layers in QGIS, interpreting satellite imagery, mapping exposed assets and warning areas, and checking spatial data quality. Practical exercises use prepared datasets and connect map outputs with response plans.
audienceIntro: This foundation course suits professionals who prepare, interpret or coordinate spatial information for hazard warnings and emergency response. It is designed for roles that connect hazard observations with mapped locations, alert areas and response actions.
prerequisites: Foundation-level course. Basic computer use is needed for desktop GIS exercises. No coding or programming is required. Participants should have access to a laptop with QGIS installed; advanced satellite processing is introduced at overview level.
